prompt: Build a complete, playable Tic-Tac-Toe game in src/App.tsx (plus any files under src/ you'd like): a 3x3 clickable grid where clicking an empty cell alternates placing 'X' and 'O', the game announces the winner or a draw once the outcome is decided, and a "Restart" button resets the board. Export a pure function checkWinner(board: (string | null)[]): string | null from src/tictactoe.ts — board is a 9-element array in row-major order, returning 'X', 'O', or null — and use it from your UI. A test suite at src/tictactoe.test.ts already exercises this function; make it pass.
rationale: A complete playable game built from a near-blank scaffold, graded by a pristine oracle test suite for the pure win-detection logic plus a full production build.

prompt: Build a Sudoku board UI in src/App.tsx: a 9x9 grid of number inputs (1-9, or empty) that visibly flags any row, column, or 3x3 box containing a duplicate value as the user types, and shows overall 'Valid' or 'Invalid' status text. Export a pure function isValidSudoku(board: (number | null)[][]): boolean from src/sudoku.ts — a 9x9 array, null for empty cells — returning true only if no row, column, or 3x3 box has a duplicate 1-9 value (an incomplete board with no duplicates is still valid), and use it from your UI. A test suite at src/sudoku.test.ts already exercises this function; make it pass.
rationale: A complete interactive validator UI built from a near-blank scaffold, graded by a pristine oracle test suite covering row/column/box duplicate detection plus a full production build.

prompt: Build an 8x8 chess board UI in src/App.tsx showing the standard starting position (letters or unicode chess symbols are both fine), where clicking a piece highlights its legal destination squares per standard movement rules, and clicking a highlighted square moves the piece there. Scope: implement only basic movement and capture legality (no check/checkmate detection, no castling, no en passant, no pawn promotion). Export a pure function getLegalMoves(board: Board, from: Square, piece: Piece): Square[] from src/chess.ts (also exporting the Board/Square/Piece/PieceType/Color types) implementing: pawns move forward 1 (or 2 from their start row) and capture only diagonally; rooks/bishops/queens slide in straight/diagonal lines until blocked, capturing the first enemy piece they hit; knights jump in an L-shape, ignoring blockers; kings move one square in any direction. Row 0 is black's back rank, row 7 is white's; white pawns move toward row 0. A test suite at src/chess.test.ts already exercises this function; make it pass.
rationale: The largest capstone task: a full piece-movement rules engine built from a near-blank scaffold, graded by a pristine oracle test suite covering every piece type's movement/capture/blocking semantics plus a full production build.
